true_summary: This diff replaces physical CSS directional properties with their logical equivalents across seven client-side files to fix RTL (right-to-left) layout issues. In show-settings.css, padding-left is replaced with padding-inline-start in two rules, a shorthand padding is decomposed into padding-block and padding-inline, and a new [dir='rtl'] rule is added to flip the active-item box-shadow to the correct edge. In header.css, three instances of left on .skip-to-content-button are replaced with inset-inline-start. In camper.css, right is replaced with inset-inline-end, margin-left with margin-inline-start, and margin-right with margin-inline-end. In experience-display.tsx and portfolio-projects.tsx, inline React styles use marginInlineStart instead of marginLeft. In toggle-setting.css, left: -9999px becomes inset-inline-start: -9999px. In sidebar-panel.css, border-right becomes border-inline-end. In super-block-accordion.css, two padding-left: 0 rules become padding-inline-start: 0, two left positional values become inset-inline-start, a new .tags-wrapper rule sets padding-inline: 64px 10px (replacing an implicit left-only padding), and a new [dir='rtl'] block is added to apply transform: rotate(-90deg) on collapsed dropdown icons for chapter, module, and block headers. In super-block-search.css, left on the magnifier icon becomes inset-inline-start and right on the reset button becomes inset-inline-end.
undisclosed_changes: In show-settings.css, the shorthand `padding: 0 1rem 0rem 2rem` is decomposed into `padding-block: 0` and `padding-inline: 2rem 1rem`, which reverses the inline start/end values compared to the original (original had padding-left 2rem, padding-right 1rem; new has padding-inline-start 2rem, padding-inline-end 1rem) — the description does not call out this specific padding decomposition.

In super-block-accordion.css, a new `.super-block-accordion .module-panel .accordion-block-expanded .tags-wrapper { padding-inline: 64px 10px }` rule is added — this is a net-new rule with a specific hard-coded 64px value, not merely a logical replacement of an existing physical property, and is not explicitly mentioned in the PR description.

The [dir='rtl'] dropdown icon rotation rule in super-block-accordion.css uses rotate(-90deg) for the collapsed state, which is the mirror of the LTR rotate(90deg) — the description mentions fixing dropdown icons but does not describe this specific transform direction detail.

In toggle-setting.css, `left: -9999px` (used to visually hide a radio input off-screen) is changed to `inset-inline-start: -9999px` — the description does not mention this accessibility/visually-hidden pattern change.
predicted_questions: In show-settings.css (padding decomposition), the logical shorthand `padding-inline: 2rem 1rem` maps inline-start to 2rem and inline-end to 1rem — identical to the original LTR physical values. Was the start/end order intentionally preserved, or was the mapping accidentally swapped given that CSS logical shorthand is start-first?

In show-settings.css, an explicit `[dir='rtl']` rule is added to flip the box-shadow active-item highlight. Why was this done with a direction-specific selector rather than using a logical approach (e.g., border-inline-start) that would avoid needing a separate RTL override entirely?

In super-block-accordion.css, a `[dir='rtl']` rule is added to rotate .dropdown-icon to -90deg for collapsed buttons. Is there a corresponding [dir='rtl'] rule for the *expanded* state icon, or will expanded icons in RTL render incorrectly?

In super-block-accordion.css, a new rule targets `.tags-wrapper` with `padding-inline: 64px 10px`. This does not appear to be a 1:1 replacement of an existing physical property — what is the origin of the 64px value, and was an equivalent rule previously defined elsewhere that was missed?

The PR description states 'LTR was measured alongside RTL on every change and is unchanged.' Are there automated visual regression or RTL-specific integration tests covering these components, or is this assurance based solely on manual testing?

true_summary: Fixes a race condition in the settings page scroll handler. `handleHashChange` in `show-settings.tsx` is changed to accept an optional `HashChangeEvent` parameter; when the event is present it reads `new URL(event.newURL).hash` rather than `window.location.hash`, making the hash read atomic with respect to the event. Adds 3 lines, deletes 2. No other files are touched.
undisclosed_changes: The PR description frames this purely as a race-condition / E2E-test fix. It does not mention that the function's call signature changes (from `() => {}` to `(event?: HashChangeEvent) => {}`), which is a breaking change if any caller passes no argument — though in practice the `hashchange` event listener passes the event object, so callers are fine.
The description mentions an E2E test was failing but does not state what the test was or whether any test file was modified. The diff shows no test changes, so coverage of the fix is implicit only.
predicted_questions: The `hashchange` event listener will now receive the `HashChangeEvent` object; but there may be other direct (non-event) call sites for `handleHashChange` that pass no argument. Were those audited to ensure they still work with `window.location.hash` as the fallback?

Using `new URL(event.newURL).hash` means the hash is read from the event's captured URL, not the live DOM. Is there a scenario where `event.newURL` could be empty or malformed and cause `new URL(...)` to throw?
The description says this 'fixed the E2E test'; which specific E2E test was flaking, and does it now pass deterministically on CI or only locally?

true_summary: Replaces named imports from JSON modules with default-import-then-destructure across 12 files in `client/src/` and 2 files in `client/tools/`, plus 2 files in `tools/client-plugins/` and 1 in `packages/challenge-builder/src/`. The pattern is consistent: `import { X } from 'module.json'` becomes `import envData from 'module.json'; const { X } = envData;` (for env.json imports) and `import { version } from 'package.json'` becomes `import pkg from 'package.json'; ... pkg.version` (for package.json version imports). In `test-runner.ts`, `export { version } from '...'` is replaced with `export const version = curriculumHelpers.version;` — this changes from a re-export to a computed const export, which is a subtle semantic difference (the re-export was live binding; the const is a snapshot at module initialization time).
